steps.what: Check food storage and cooking temperatures against the applicable kitchen requirements
Regulate ovens, broilers, grills and roasters and respond to storage temperature problems

tasks.design: Keep food temperature checks and equipment regulation human, with current kitchen requirements in {DOCS} as a reference. Existing equipment controls remain in place; no remote control or reduction in actual checking is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: An equipment setting alone does not establish the temperature of the food.
tasks.enabler_now: Current temperature equipment and native kitchen instructions already support the work.
tasks.still_hard: Different food loads and equipment behaviour require observation and appropriate response.
tasks.human_edge: The cook notices when the food or equipment is not behaving as expected.
tasks.altitude: Temperature-checking effort and responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Respond to food temperature concerns during service

evidence.claim: Food temperature checks and physical equipment regulation require actual observation; no saving is claimed from existing thermostats or logging tools.

assumptions: Boundary is checking actual food temperatures and regulating cooking or responding to storage problems, excluding separate record transcription, maintenance and developing the kitchen's safety requirements.

Kitchen management supplies applicable instructions through existing work. Cook produces readings through direct checking in s1 and responds in s2, with all time retained; no free structured correct-temperature flag is assumed.
Formal record entry belongs to the separately owned records task and is counted once. Keep native equipment and current practice, with no new sensor or process and zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Applicable kitchen instructions and equipment types
research_questions: Can staff distinguish an equipment setting from an actual food temperature check and follow the existing escalation route?

already_counted.description: Check actual temperatures and regulate or escalate equipment conditions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Physical checks and regulation keep full time; existing equipment runtime earns no human saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check freshness and rotate food stock

steps.what: Check freshness and quality of food and ingredients and distinguish old and new stock
Rotate stock and handle ingredients that do not meet freshness or quality requirements

tasks.design: Keep freshness assessment and physical stock rotation human, using current label and kitchen guidance in {DOCS} where required. A date record supports the cook's inspection but does not establish that an ingredient is suitable.
tasks.previous_blocker: Freshness and condition depend on the actual food and its handling history.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing labels and native kitchen guidance already support the task.
tasks.still_hard: A labelled item can still be damaged or inconsistent with the expected quality.
tasks.human_edge: The cook notices actual condition and takes appropriate action rather than trusting a date alone.
tasks.altitude: Inspection and stock rotation time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Handle ingredient stock in the correct sequence

evidence.claim: Ingredient freshness checking and stock rotation require observation and physical handling; no labour saving is claimed.

assumptions: Boundary is freshness assessment and physical rotation, excluding purchasing, forecasting, receiving deliveries and separate administrative record entry. Count shared stock inspection once.

Suppliers and receiving staff produce existing date and batch labels through unchanged delivery handling. Cook checks their relevance and actual food condition within s1's 60 hours; missing or conflicting labels follow current manual clarification rather than a machine inference.
Cook produces rotation decisions during s1 and implements them in s2's retained 40 hours. No free structured freshness flag or automated physical movement is assumed.
Keep native guidance and labels. No new recording requirement, camera or stock process means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: How reliable existing stock labels are
Which quality concerns need specialist or supervisor decisions
research_questions: Does actual stock inspection detect condition problems that date labels alone would miss?

already_counted.description: Inspect food condition, decide rotation and physically handle stock

incremental.description: No new freshness or rotation process upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Freshness checks and physical stock handling retain full time; no supplier or equipment runtime saving is claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Coordinate and supervise work of kitchen staff and resolve changing service priorities

tasks.design: Keep kitchen coordination and supervision human, with existing service information in {OPS_SYSTEM} where currently used. The cook responds to actual preparation progress and staff concerns during service.
tasks.previous_blocker: Kitchen dependencies change quickly and require shared understanding among people working together.
tasks.enabler_now: Current native service records and direct communication already support the task.
tasks.still_hard: A nominal task list cannot show every readiness, quality or staffing problem.
tasks.human_edge: The cook notices pressure and coordinates practical help at the right moment.
tasks.altitude: Supervision time and authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Lead a kitchen team through changing service demand

evidence.claim: Kitchen supervision is contextual interpersonal work; no labour saving is inferred from task-board or scheduling capability.

assumptions: Boundary is coordination and supervision itself, excluding roster administration, cooking execution and separate safety checks. Shared supervisory actions must have one owner across cook and chef roles.

Service staff produce orders through normal service and kitchen workers produce progress and concerns through actual work. Cook elicits, checks and communicates guidance within the retained 100 hours; no free structured readiness or worker-performance flag is assumed.
Keep native service records and current communication. No tracking, automated allocation or new process means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Division of authority between cook and head cook
Which service dependencies cause recurring coordination problems
research_questions: Do staff understand the current priorities and when to ask for help during service?

already_counted.description: Observe kitchen work, coordinate priorities and supervise staff

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Coordination and supervision keep full effort; staff execution is outside the focal denominator.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Capture required kitchen records and accounts from observed activity and supporting receipts
Copy kitchen entries into parallel account sheets and record summaries
Check records and accounts against actual activity and resolve missing entries or discrepancies
outputs: accepted kitchen records and account summary

tasks.design: Configure one-entry kitchen forms in {WORKFLOW}, with native record views and account exports replacing a parallel {SPREADSHEET} list. The cook still captures actual observations and receipts and checks completeness and exceptions before accepting the record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper entries were re-entered into several record and account summaries.
tasks.enabler_now: Native kitchen registration tools support recorded measurements and missing-entry notifications; ordinary account exports can reuse the same captured entries.
tasks.still_hard: A completed form does not establish that the observation happened or that all costs and usage were recorded.
tasks.human_edge: The cook knows the actual kitchen activity and recognises misleading or incomplete entries.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate entry where it exists; observation capture and record responsibility remain human.

reach.task: Review kitchen usage and operating records
reach.learn: Source completeness and meaningful variance investigation

evidence.claim: Hygiënecode Online supports kitchen hygiene registrations and warnings for missed measurements; this supports testing native registration, not automatic food-safety conclusions or account integration.
The proposed single-entry account export and task savings are unmeasured model scenarios.

assumptions: Boundary is administrative capture and checking of kitchen records and accounts, excluding physical temperature checks, stock inspection, cooking, payment processing and formal financial statements. Allocate each observation and entry once across tasks; a kitchen already capturing once has no s2 saving.

Cook produces entry identifier, activity date and time, record type, source document reference, item or location, observed value and unit, purchase or usage quantity and amount where relevant, and correction note in s1's retained 30 hours. Physical observations are produced by separately owned normal kitchen work; their time is not removed or counted again as a saving.

Kitchen management supplies existing required fields and bookkeepers supply existing account categories. Additional export-field and category upkeep is counted below. Views replacing s2 consume only the captured entries; no free structured discrepancy or safe-food flag is assumed.

Missing observations, uncertain categories or unsupported documents return to manual recording and reconciliation in s3's retained 45 hours. No model invents readings or reconciles away missing evidence.

Try native forms and exports before custom code. Applicable record and national consultation requirements need customer confirmation; s3 accepts an exact record with unresolved questions visible, not automatic safety certification.
unknowns: Which records and accounts the cook personally maintains
Whether native forms and exports cover the required records
research_questions: Can the kitchen capture once while preserving actual observation evidence and reconciling all required records?

already_counted.description: Capture record fields and check completeness and discrepancies including manual fallback

incremental.description: Maintain entry forms and check account export mappings
Maintain additional bookkeeping category and export configuration

approvals.approved_version: Exact kitchen record and account summary version, source entries, supporting receipts and unresolved questions; changes void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=75, gross=25; subtract 8 focal upkeep for central net=17. Range assumes only some duplicate record entry is removable and unsupported records remain manual. Three other-role upkeep hours are recorded separately; observation capture and physical checks keep full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Duplicate record copying may shrink, while food checks, stock rotation and kitchen supervision retain full human time.
reach: Improve record review and coordination with chefs and head cooks
Discuss ingredient handling with food preparation workers
skills_to_grow: Distinguish actual observations from completed forms
Capture source fields once and reconcile exceptions
role.ambitious_version: Maintain dependable kitchen records while protecting the hands-on judgement and coordination that food preparation requires.
